ported_content.name: SetItem (SetItem enum, ISetItem, SetHelper)

Deviations D-2 and D-4 in notes/s1-armour-sets.md.

ported_content.name: BaseSetArmor
ported_content.note: The key design decision of S1. ServUO puts set state on BaseArmor itself; doing that in ModernUO would mean bumping BaseArmor's [SerializationGenerator(9)] to 10 and owning a migration for an upstream file. Instead this additive abstract class at version 0 carries the state and set content derives from it. Behaviourally identical for set content, because no stock ModernUO armour is a set item (verified at runtime).

ported_content.name: PlayerMobile set resistances
ported_content.note: Additive partial class, no patch needed: PlayerMobile is already partial and is not source-generated. Overrides the GetItemResistance virtual that Mobile-set-item-resistance-hook.patch introduces.

ported_content.name: TigerPelt armour (8 files)
ported_content.note: CC3 called these 'itself set-bonus content'. That was wrong: grep SetID over all eight returns nothing. They are plain BaseArmor leaf armour and were never blocked. Ported unchanged, re-parented to BaseSetArmor so the Aloron pieces that derive from them can carry set state. Weight moves from a ctor assignment to a DefaultWeight override, the ModernUO idiom.

ported_content.name: Aloron's Armor set (8 files)
ported_content.note: The CC3 decline, reversed. Four-piece set (SetItem.Aloron), SetAttributes BonusMana 15 / LowerManaCost 20, SetSelfRepair 3, per-piece resist bonuses 8/8/9/8/8. Verified at runtime: four pieces worn gives 60/60/60/60/60 resists and BonusMana 15 through AosAttributes.GetValue. Two deviations: AbsorptionAttributes.EaterCold=2 omitted (SAAbsorptionAttributes is a separate missing subsystem that drags in three more), and the Dinosaur Slayer omitted along with its tooltip line, rather than advertise a bonus that does nothing. D-1 and D-2 in notes/s1-armour-sets.md.

ported_content.name: FountainOfFortune
ported_content.note: BaseAddon with a reward loop, three static tables, a defrag timer and a resurrect hook. Subsystem-shaped, so it ships with a test per docs/subsystem-policy.md - the first content task to use S4's route. Needs server/patches/PlayerMobile-fountain-luck-bonus.patch: ServUO routes the luck reward through PlayerMobile.RealLuck, which ModernUO does not have, and its three luck consumers all read Mobile.Luck. ModernUO's ResurrectGump takes no callback, so FountainResurrectGump subclasses it rather than patching upstream. Two reward cases are unreachable in ServUO too (Random(4) over a six-case switch) and were ported unchanged. NOTHING PLACES ONE: ServUO builds it in Services/Underworld/Generate.cs, which is not ported. Q-021.

ported_content.name: GemologistsSatchel

Not a subsystem pull-in - all 35 are leaf items - so all 35 were ported (Q-020, Chase chose option A). ported_content.name: SolesOfProvidence

ported_content.name: Imbuing ingredient set (35 leaf items)
ported_content.source: ServUO Scripts/Items/Resource/ (31 files, 1,668 lines) plus MagicalResidue, EnchantedEssence, RelicFragment and BouraPelt in Scripts/Items/Quest/SAQuestItems.cs

declined_content.name: ServUO ML quest framework - decline REAFFIRMED by S5
declined_content.reason: S5 translated one quest end to end and the objective mapping holds for 4 of 5 types, two of them pinned by tests. Porting ServUO's 22-file, 6,269-line framework would put a second engine in the tree to do a job the engine we already have does correctly. The decline was always on two-engines-for-one-job; it now rests on measurement rather than on principle alone. What is NOT declined: the 164 of 203 missing quests that use a single standard objective type. The 39 that hand-write a BaseObjective subclass (25 InternalObjective, 3 CollectionsObtain, 2 QuestionAndAnswer, ~9 one-offs) are per-quest work, not a framework port, and are the thing to cost before the next quest batch.

tasks.title: Test route for ported subsystems
tasks.note: server/tests/<path> mirrors into Projects/UOContent.Tests/Tests/<path> through mirror_cs_tree(), the same F2 mechanism structured customizations use, with the same destination-must-not-already-exist guard. S1's tests are committed and green - four [Fact] methods, not the six docs/tasks.md claims (Q-019). Three of the four fail docker build itself; a failing assertion fails docker/uo/build.sh, because every ModernUO fixture needs io_uring and docker build cannot relax seccomp (Q-018). build.sh is now the build command. tasks.title: Translate one ML quest onto ModernUO's engine
tasks.note: JourneyToTheAthenaeumIsleQuest translated onto ModernUO's ML quest engine end to end. 6 files, 1,063 ServUO lines in, 745 out, plus a 284-line test with 5 facts. Gated build green at 14 tests. THE MAPPING HOLDS for 4 of 5 objective types: Slay->Kill and Obtain->Collect are identical and are proven by test; Apprentice->GainSkill holds (upstream already made this exact translation in NewHavenSkillTraining.cs) but loses region-scoped acceleration and needs cap x10; Deliver->Deliver holds but the destination name moves to a [QuesterName] attribute and Quest.StartingItem has no counterpart (Q-025); Escort->Escort holds and its dropped fame/compassion parameters are unused across all 30 ServUO call sites. THE REAL FINDING is not the mapping: of the 203 missing quests, 164 use one standard objective type and translate mechanically, but 39 hand-write a BaseObjective subclass with no counterpart - 25 of them InternalObjective. QuestionAndAnswerObjective is 2 of those 39, not the tail. Also: it is the ONLY quest in all 408 that uses two standard objective types, and Valley of One is a poor first batch (3 of its 7 need a hand-written objective). Registration uses MLQuestSystem.Register rather than Data/MLQuests.cfg, which apply-patches.sh cannot carry; that API has zero upstream callers, so a test guards it. Found a gap in the S4 route: no BaseCreature can be constructed in a test without the npc-speeds.json table (Q-026). Answers Q-023. See notes/s5-quest-spike.md.
